turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it: on what basis did my son get a zero, and why did he find out on his phone in the middle of class?
I spoke with the vice principal before you came in.
The vice principal. So now two people have discussed my son before anyone spoke to me, and that's going in my notes. Did anyone speak to Owen before that zero went in, yes or no?
She's backing me completely. Policy is policy, and it isn't up to you.

"Policy is policy." Good, I printed it: 4.2 says you contact the parent before any mark consequence is entered, and 4.3 says software alone doesn't establish a concern. If the vice principal is backing a zero that skipped both, I'll want that in writing from her, today.
So frankly, this meeting is a courtesy.

"A courtesy." Under 4.2 it was supposed to happen before the zero, Hale, not a week after it. Either show me what you have on Owen's essay besides a machine's score, or I'm walking down the hall to the principal's office when we're done here.
